title: Integral logarithmic pullback at nodal images, including persistent nodes
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be projective flat finitely presented morphisms whose geometric fibres are nonempty connected reduced curves of pure dimension one with only ordinary double points. Give them pairwise disjoint sections $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ in the relative smooth loci, with $n\geq0$. The meanings of marked nodal family and of its canonically normalized dualizing invertible module are those of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]. Put $D_X=\sum_j a_j(S)$, $D_Y=\sum_j b_j(S)$ and $L_X=\omega_{X/R}(D_X)$, $L_Y=\omega_{Y/R}(D_Y)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let $p:Y\to X$ be an $S$-morphism with $p b_j=a_j$ and assume $p_K:Y_K\to X_K$ is an isomorphism. Let $M=(p^*L_X)^\vee\otimes L_Y$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module], and let $s_K\in\Gamma(Y_K,M|_{Y_K})$ be the section corresponding to the canonical logarithmic-dualizing pullback isomorphism of $p_K$. For a generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $Y_k$, set $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ and regard the germ of $s_K$ as an element of $M_\eta[1/\pi]$; this is restriction to the inverse image of $Y_K$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $x=p(\eta)$ is not relatively smooth in $X/S$, then $s_K$ belongs to the image of $M_\eta\to M_\eta[1/\pi]$. This integrality is with respect to the original canonical adjunction normalization, before any etale chart choices. In particular it holds if a node persists on the generic fibre: an etale local chart $uv=h$ may have $h=0$, and either pullback coordinate may vanish identically on one generic branch. Here an ordinary double point means a nonsmooth geometric fibre point with completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, as in the marked-family convention above. No smoothness of $X_K$ or $Y_K$, normality of $X$ or $Y$, properness of $p$, or positivity is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family); agent branch-integrality and faithfully flat pole-quotient argument from old lem-sfb-nodal-log-dualizing-pullback Steps 2, 3, 6 and 7. Normalization uses duality.tex lemma-fundamental-class-lci and lemma-shriek-etale. Not a verbatim assertion of the tag.

proof.text: Work at the given $\eta$. The Noetherian hypotheses hold: $R$ is Noetherian and $X/R$ and $Y/R$ are of finite type, so both total spaces are Noetherian. The generic-fibre-points-smooth lemma applies to $Y/R$, since every geometric fibre is reduced; hence $Y/R$ is smooth on a neighbourhood of $\eta$. Shrink that neighbourhood inside the complement of $D_Y$. This is possible because each marking meets the one-dimensional special fibre in a closed point, whereas $\eta$ is a component generic point. Likewise $x=p(\eta)$ is disjoint from $D_X$, since every $a_j$ lies in the smooth locus whereas $x$ does not. We may remove $D_X$ and its inverse image. Thus both logarithmic twists are canonically trivial on the neighbourhoods used below.

source.place: Tag 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open), together with morphisms.tex Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point); agent unmarked-neighbourhood reduction

proof.text: The smooth-trait local-properties lemma makes $A=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ a Noetherian local domain. By the fibre-stalk quotient formula, $A/\pi A=\mathcal O_{Y_k,\eta}$. This is a field: in a reduced scheme the localization at a minimal prime has its only prime equal to zero, since its nilradical is zero. Thus $\mathfrak m_A=\pi A$. Flatness makes $\pi$ a nonzero divisor, and $\pi$ is a nonunit at $\eta$. The principal-ideal DVR criterion now makes $A$ a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$. Write $F=A[1/\pi]=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The smooth-locus dualizing identification and the differential-stalk formula identify $(L_Y)_\eta$ with $\Omega_{A/R}$, a free rank-one $A$-module.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), together with schemes.tex Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre); agent local calculation

proof.text: Choose a nodal chart at $x$ by the trait nodal etale DVR model: an injective local etale extension $R\to R\prime$ with the same uniformizer $\pi$, and etale maps $U\to X$, $U\to C=\operatorname{Spec}(R\prime[u,v]/(uv-h))$, with a point above $x$, where $h=0$ or $h=\pi^n$. Shrink $U$ to an affine neighbourhood of that point; all comparisons below may be restricted further. Form $T=Y\times_XU$. A point $t\in T$ above $\eta$ and that chart point exists: the tensor product of their residue fields over $\kappa(x)$ is nonzero. The projection $e:T\to Y$ is etale. Restrict $T$ to the inverse image of the smooth neighbourhood from Step 1 and then to an affine neighbourhood of $t$. All etale source maps so used are finitely presented, since the schemes are Noetherian and the chosen affine neighbourhoods are quasi-compact.

Put $B=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Since $e$ is etale and $Y/R$ is smooth of relative dimension one near $\eta$, smooth relative-dimension permanence makes $T/R$ smooth of relative dimension one near $t$. The smooth-trait local-properties lemma makes $B$ a Noetherian local domain. The local map $A\to B$ is flat, hence faithfully flat by the flat-local-hom lemma. Its closed fibre is the local ring at a point of an etale scheme over $A/\pi A$, a field. The etale-fibre dimension lemma gives dimension zero; etale morphisms are smooth, and smooth morphisms have geometrically reduced fibres, so this local fibre ring is reduced. A zero-dimensional reduced local ring is a field. Therefore $\mathfrak m_B=\pi B$, and the principal-ideal criterion makes $B$ a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$. Set $E=B[1/\pi]$. In particular $E$ is a field and is the generic local ring of $T$ through $t$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); morphisms.tex Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); agent etale stalk calculation

proof.text: Use the canonical adjunction line of the model $C/R\prime$. The equation $uv-h$ is a nonzero divisor (it is monic in the monomial $uv$), so this is a regular hypersurface presentation. Its monomial normal forms $1,u^i,v^j$ ($i,j>0$) give a free $R\prime$-module, hence flatness; a geometric fibre is a hyperbola or two coordinate lines, hence pure one-dimensional. The signed-Jacobian formula gives an integral frame $\lambda$ of that line with $\alpha(du)=u\lambda$ and $\alpha(dv)=-v\lambda$: for the ordering $(u,v)$ the two determinants are $-u$ and $v$, and replace the determinant frame by its negative. Consequently $\lambda=du/u$ on $D(u)$ and $\lambda=-dv/v$ on $D(v)$. The canonical etale-source adjunction comparisons transport this integral frame to a frame of $\omega_{U/R\prime}$, and the base-change comparison transports the original normalized $\omega_{X/R}$ first to $X\times_R R\prime$ and then to $U$. Here $U\to X\times_R R\prime$ is etale by etale composition cancellation, since both its composite to $X$ and the projection to $X$ are etale. They agree with differential pullback on the relative smooth locus. The lci hypotheses for $X$ are supplied by the nodal-family regular-presentation lemma. Thus this is a frame in the original normalized line after etale pullback, not a rationally rescaled line.

Let $a,b\in B$ be the pullbacks of $u,v$. At least one is nonzero in $E$. Indeed $T_K\simeq U_K$ because $p_K$ is an isomorphism, and $T$ is smooth over $R$ near $t$. For the etale map $R\to R\prime$, $\Omega_{R\prime/R}=0$. Every $R$-derivation of a $R\prime$-algebra therefore kills $R\prime$, by restricting it to $R\prime$ and using the universal property; this identifies relative differential modules over $R$ and $R\prime$. If $a=b=0$ in $E$, the presentation $R\prime[u,v]/(uv-h)$ has, after tensoring with $E$, two independent differentials $du,dv$, because its sole relation is $v\,du+u\,dv=0$. The formally-etale differential base-change isomorphism for $U\to C$ would then give dimension two for the differentials of $U_K$ at this point. But $U_K\simeq T_K$ is smooth of relative dimension one and has differential dimension one. This contradiction proves the assertion. This calculation also applies when $h=0$; it never requires both coordinates to be nonzero.

source.place: Etale differential base change and Tag 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize); agent nonzero-branch argument using the relation v du+u dv

proof.text: Choose the nonzero coordinate. If $a\ne0$, the DVR uniformizer-power lemma gives $a=\pi^m w$ with $m\ge0$ and $w\in B^\times$. The universal derivation over $R\prime$ kills $\pi$, so in $\Omega_{E/R\prime}$ one has $da/a=w^{-1}dw$. Thus $da/a$ is the localization of an element of $\Omega_{B/R\prime}$. If instead $a=0$, Step 6 gives $b\ne0$; write $b=\pi^m w$ and use $-db/b=-w^{-1}dw$. By Step 5 and the ordinary differential pullback on the smooth generic locus, the chosen differential is exactly the image of the original chart frame under the canonical generic comparison. In particular, when $h=0$ and one coordinate vanishes identically on this branch, only the other coordinate is divided by.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), uniformizer-power formula; elementary Leibniz calculation over R′

proof.text: The differential in Step 7 determines an integral homomorphism from the pulled-back source line to the target line at $t$: send the transported frame $\lambda$ to that differential. The differential-stalk formula identifies the latter with the stalk of $\Omega^1_{T/R\prime}$. The canonical etale-source adjunction isomorphisms, applied to $e:T\to Y$ (affine, hence finitely presented, and etale) with the regular affine presentations of $Y/R$ supplied by the nodal-family regular-presentation lemma, which applies to $Y$ exactly as to $X$ in Step 5, identify the target line with the pullback of $L_Y$; the base-change normalization for $R\prime/R$ is the same as that used for $X$ in Step 5. Hence this homomorphism is an element of $B\otimes_A M_\eta$, and its image after inverting $\pi$ is $1\otimes s_K$. Equality here is tested over $E$, where $T_K\simeq U_K$ and all points involved are relatively smooth; every comparison is the usual differential pullback there. The twists were removed canonically in Step 1, so no marking or normalization factor remains.

source.place: Tags 0FWI (lemma-shriek-etale) and 0E9Z (lemma-fundamental-class-lci); elementary assembly with the specified normalized comparisons

proof.text: Descend to $A$ without descending either chart frame. Trivialize the rank-one module $M_\eta$ and write its generic element as $c/\pi^N$ with $c\in A$. Step 8 says its image in $E$ lies in $B$. Since $B$ has no $\pi$-torsion, this means $c\in\pi^N B$. Apply faithful-flat universal injectivity to the $A$-module $A/\pi^N A$: its class maps to zero in $B/\pi^N B$, so $c\in\pi^N A$. Therefore $c/\pi^N\in A$, as required. The conclusion concerns the original $s_K$, since only its own scalar extension was tested. This proves the stated image condition, including $h=0$ and $n=0$ markings. No normality of either total space, properness of $p$, or smoothness of an entire generic fibre has been used.
